note: Permission words that exist on one side only: offered to the owner and asked for by nothing, or demanded by a door and offered to nobody. The vocabulary this gate reads is the AGENT consent screen (public/views/profile/agents/scope-model.js), which is the list an owner ticks when connecting an agent. A word belonging to a different grant path is not a defect and belongs here with the path named. A word in this file is otherwise a question nobody has answered, not a clearance.

exempt.demanded:events:emit: REVIEWED 2026-09-04, and it is meant to exist on one side only. The door is POST /v1/ecosystem/events (src/routes/ecosystem-events.ts:53) and it is gated requireRole('ecosystem') BEFORE requireScope, so the only principal that reaches it is a GEAI. An ecosystem app does not get its scopes from the agent consent screen: it declares them at hello, the owner narrows them at approve, and they are pinned into the token with a data-area allowlist (docs/building-an-aimeat-compatible-ecosystem-app.md). Putting `events:emit` on the agent screen would offer a human the power to let an AGENT emit ecosystem events, which is not a thing that exists. The gate reports it because it reads one of the two vocabularies; teaching it the ecosystem one is worth doing the day a second word appears here, and not before.
exempt.demanded:contract:spend: REVIEWED 2026-10-12, and it is meant to exist on one side only. It is an APP GRANT word (src/routes/app-grant-vocabulary.ts: 'Buy on your behalf using contracts you hold'), offered on the app consent screen and never on the agent one. The three doors that name it are the checkout completions and the app-store purchase, gated requireRestScope('commerce:buy', { orScope: 'contract:spend' }): an agent pays on commerce:buy, the word its MCP twin aimeat_checkout_complete asks, and an app on contract:spend, the word completeSession already asks of an app grant inside the service (appSpendRefusal in src/commerce/session-service.ts). Putting contract:spend on the agent screen would give agents a second word for the same spend.
